# M0-s-02: closing check of hardening round S1 (lane `check/M0-s-02-close-s1`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-21)

The seat ran in a Claude Code cloud container: Opus 5.5, Linux x64, Node v24.12.0. The machine check
(`tools/machine_profile.py --id`) printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which matches the
brief. `tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 (and `--mutants` 1) before the runs, so every vitest run used
`--maxWorkers=1` and the mutants ran one at a time. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker (J162), independent
of the round: it is not the round's builder (L-0605, `build/M0-s-02-fix-s1`), the item's author (L-0078) or an earlier
fixer or checker of the item. Its ledger row is L-0606 in `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2. The lane log had no line for this lane
key and no earlier session round (`-s0`) of the item exists, so the seat started fresh. This is the third part of merged
round M3 (after M0-f-03a's S4 and M0-f-02a's S1).

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote this file, the notes section 'Hardening round S1 — the closing check's
  notes' (N14, N15) in `checks/M0-s-02-notes.md`, its CLEAN-ROOM row, its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It
  ran no git command.
* **Files under check.** The item's 33 files in the tree hash to the landed record `landed/M0-s-02.json` (33 / 33, a
  Python `sha256` over the record's list). The record's changed source files for this round are
  `src/loader/view.ts` and `src/loader/table.ts`; the five handed-over data files (granularity, regimes, interior, cut,
  bands) are not in the record because they resolve to their receivers at flow-7 (C-0318; see N-10 below).
* **Mirror.** `/home/user/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-s-02/mirror/`, a `cp -a` of `plat/` (0 symbolic links resolving
  outside it; the workspace links are relative). Baseline `test/{cell,loader,data}` at W = 1: 210 / 210. Every mutant
  and plant was applied by a script (`mut.py`, outside the mirror), run with `--bail=1` and restored from the tree with
  a `cmp` check.
* **Before-images.** No git command was run, so the seat holds no before-image of the round's files. In its place
  each fix is reverted in the mirror as a mutant (the registration ignored, the class fields back, the grammars
  admitting '/', the N1 law disabled with the fixed pins re-gated on the golden version, the N2 snapshots made exact at
  every version): those are the "red without the fix" receipts below.
* **Disclosure.** Reading `checks/M0-s-02-notes.md` whole (the brief's instruction for the source notes N1 and N2)
  also took in the builder's 'Hardening round S1' section, which lists its plants and mutant ids; the resume-rule grep
  of the lane log printed the builder's CHECKPOINT and LANDED lines. The builder's self-check folder was not opened.
  This seat's probes were planned from the source notes, the inventory rows and the code; they overlap the builder's
  where the promise is the same, and add the real-data plants (the builder's were partly in-memory), the lawful
  real-data hand-overs L1 – L7, the reverted-pin runs, S7 – S9, N4c, T13, T14, W2, C3, X3 and the census probe of its
  own. The harness put the user's account e-mail and a git attribution note in this seat's context unasked; neither
  was used.

## Verdict: PASS

N1 and N2 are FIXED and PINNED: every escape the source notes name is red now and passes with the pins reverted, and
every lawful hand-over (including additions) is green now and red under the old exact snapshots. M0-c-05's N-10 stays
REPORTED for a confirmed ownership reason, with its declared shift measured. e-04 s3's N-s3c-3 registration half is
FIXED and PINNED; its composer half is REPORTED to the layout owners. L22's N4 is FIXED and PINNED, N6 PINNED, N7 FIXED
(comment). Every gate is green. The refusal census did not rise (lawful 0 → 0). No blocker; two new hardening notes
(N14, N15).

## (4) New findings (blocker rule)

No blocker. Two hardening notes, appended to `checks/M0-s-02-notes.md` and recorded as `check-M0-s-02-notes`:

* **N14** — `tableView`'s registration check is `instanceof Table`, and `Table` (exported) has a constructor that
  checks nothing: a hand-built `new Table('s6', raw)` with a unit-less cell is accepted (probe CONFIRMED). No source
  constructs a `Table` outside `parseTable` (grep), so only a deliberate writer reaches it. M4.
* **N15** — the hand-over law does not hold a handed-over table's `section` field to its version-1 text. Metadata
  only, outside the pinning hash. M4.
